html:
The Simba rebellion was a rising in the eastern and central Congo in 1964 and 1965 by followers of the murdered Patrice Lumumba, whose fighters called themselves simba, lions.

The rebels, who believed charms made them bulletproof, swept across much of the country and took Stanleyville, now Kisangani, where they declared a people's republic and held hundreds of white residents hostage.

In November 1964, Belgian paratroopers dropped from American planes in Operation Dragon Rouge freed most of the hostages, while white mercenaries and government troops under Tshombe retook the towns. Che Guevara joined the rebels for a time in 1965 and left disillusioned. It was the last phase of the Congo Crisis before Mobutu's coup.
sum: The Simba rebellion was a rising in the eastern and central Congo in 1964 and 1965 by followers of the murdered Patrice Lumumba, whose fighters called themselves simba, lions.
